title: State CIOs support election technology, but secretaries of state often manage the systems
summary: While secretaries of state often maintain their own election technology infrastructure, state CIOs provide support for cybersecurity, network capacity and incident response.

title: Data sharing could help states better align Medicaid and public health efforts, report finds
summary: The report highlights how stronger data-sharing partnerships between Medicaid and public health agencies could help states better identify health needs and fine tune intervention strategies.

title: Center for Civic Futures awards grant to Nava Labs to help modernize state benefits technology with AI
summary: The latest award through the organization’s Public Benefit Innovation Fund will support the use of artificial intelligence tools to help agencies update aging Medicaid and SNAP systems.

title: Report: Over 42 million records exposed by local government technology platform for civic engagement
summary: A cybersecurity researcher found millions of files exposed in a database tied to CitySourced, a civic engagement platform used by local governments.

title: Aspen Institute warns states need funding to strengthen EBT security
summary: A proposed USDA rule would require states to upgrade SNAP payment cards and implement other security measures, but the Aspen Institute says new federal mandates risk competing with costly program changes.

title: A strategic guide to digital transformation in state government
summary: Go beyond implementing new technology. Read how government leaders can leverage workforce development, automation and enterprise architecture.

title: Philadelphia launches toolkit to help neighborhoods prepare for climate risks
summary: The free resource gives residents guides and activities to organize neighborhood discussions about extreme heat, flooding and other climate-related hazards.

title: Missouri CIO set to retire at the end of the year
summary: John Laurent has served as Missouri’s chief information officer since December 2024 and calls retirement “bittersweet.”

title: More than half of K-12 schools reported cyber incidents amid staffing, funding gaps
summary: The report found that K-12 schools faced persistent cyber threats last year, while struggling with limited resources and emerging AI-related risks.

title: Georgia says Anthropic AI agent accessed public election data, not its voter registration system
summary: The secretary of state says an Anthropic AI agent accessed public election information, but did not “hack” into voter registration systems.
